EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic strong ν(C≡N) Raman band at 2255 cm⁻¹, so the molecule must contain a nitrile group. Among the candidates, compounds 1, 4, 5 and 10 have a –C≡N group; the remaining candidates have C≡C or N=N units instead. The absence of N–H stretching bands near 3300 cm⁻¹ argues against the amine-containing nitriles 4 and 10, leaving 1 and 5, which are simple aliphatic ethers bearing a terminal nitrile. The spectrum contains several C–O–C stretching bands (1024, 1070, 1127 cm⁻¹) and typical aliphatic C–H deformations (1451, 1487 cm⁻¹) consistent with an unbranched ether chain, matching 1 (CCCCO-CH₂CH₂-C≡N) better than the branched structure 5. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the observed Raman features.
